conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling now that your little one has arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted tool called the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days; it helps us pick up on signs of depression, anxiety, or distress that are surprisingly common after childbirth, and it includes a question about self-harm so we can be sure you’re safe. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell us someone is in danger. There are no right or wrong answers, and we’ll go at your pace.

To begin:  
Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve still laughed a little, mostly when my partner cracks jokes or the baby makes silly faces. It doesn’t come as easily as before I gave birth, though—sometimes I catch myself half-laughing and then feel too tired to keep it going.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most of the time I still laugh, but I don’t find things quite as funny as I used to—sometimes it feels like I’m forcing it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few things—like taking the baby for a short walk or having my morning coffee—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. Sometimes I plan an outing and then feel kind of “meh” when the time comes.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. When the baby won’t settle or I can’t figure out what he needs, I keep thinking I should just “know” already and that a “better mom” would handle it smoothly. I’ll tell myself it’s my fault for not reading enough or for being too tired to think straight. It’s not constant, but it pops up a few times a day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly feel on edge, like there’s something I’ve forgotten or that something bad could happen, even when everything’s calm. It usually passes if I take a few deep breaths or remind myself the baby’s okay, but it sneaks up a few times each day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I’ve had a couple of short moments where my heart races and I feel shaky, like I’m about to get bad news, but I can’t point to anything that triggered it. It fades after a few minutes, and it hasn’t happened every day—maybe twice this week.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, some days it feels like the dishes, the laundry, and the baby’s needs all hit at once. I’ll be feeding him and notice the clutter piling up, and suddenly feel like I’m drowning a little. I usually manage to get through it, but those waves of “I can’t keep up” happen most days.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’ve been pretty sad off and on, but once I finally lie down I still drift off. It just takes me a little longer to settle my thoughts—maybe an extra 15 or 20 minutes—but my actual sleep hasn’t suffered much.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I do feel that way—kind of heavy and down—most days. It’s not all day long; it comes in waves. I’ll be fine while the baby’s smiling, but then something small, like seeing a picture of myself before pregnancy, makes me tear up or feel blue for a while.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—usually when everything feels piled up or if the baby won’t settle and I worry I’m doing it all wrong. It’s not every day, but those tears come pretty easily once I start.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt tired and low, but hurting myself hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Screening note – 2 wk PP visit  
Patient: Postpartum parent, 2 weeks after delivery, breastfeeding, partner at work most of day.

Self-report summary (EPDS-10 themes)  
• Anhedonia: diminished ability to laugh/look forward to events; pleasure “not as strong.”  
• Persistent low mood: “heavy and down most days,” tearfulness 2× this week.  
• Guilt / self-blame: several times daily (“should be a better mom”).  
• Anxiety: daily unprovoked edginess; 2 brief panic-like episodes (HR ↑, shakes, resolves <5 min).  
• Feeling overwhelmed: daily waves of “can’t keep up” with chores plus infant care.  
• Sleep: latency ↑ 15–20 min; no frank insomnia.  
• Energy/interest: chores feel “drowning.”  
• Self-harm: denied; no suicidal ideation voiced.

Pattern: sub-syndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms; functional impact mild–moderate; no safety concerns at present.

Screening significance  
– Score pattern consistent with at least minor depression ± comorbid anxiety.  
– Continued monitoring warranted; consider full EPDS scoring and follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen, functioning declines, or SI develops.
